title: Rechargeable lithium-ion battery from high-energy intercalation to safe commercial cells
pressure: Portable electronics and energy shocks created demand for light rechargeable high-energy cells, but reactive lithium metal could short, burn or explode.
preExistingWorldModel: Lead-acid/NiCd were rechargeable but heavier/lower-energy; intercalation materials suggested reversible ion storage in host lattices.
candidateRoutes: higher-voltage oxide cathode with lithium metal
carbon host anode eliminating metallic lithium
observationsAndInstruments: Whittingham demonstrated reversible TiS2 intercalation and a high-energy rechargeable cell.
Repeated charging produced lithium whiskers/dendrites and fire risk.
Goodenough showed a higher-voltage cobalt-oxide cathode.
Yoshino paired an oxide cathode with carbonaceous anode so metallic lithium was absent.
Commercial lithium-ion cells entered the market in 1991.
decisiveTests: pass cell-level manufacturing and abuse tests
technicalOrScientificTransition: Commercial lithium-ion was a sequence of material and architecture corrections in which repeatable cycling and safety outranked locally maximal energy density.
rivalsAndFailures: The earliest high-energy rechargeable chemistry was not commercially viable because safety failed under cycling.
Sponsor incentives changed with oil prices while development moved elsewhere.
A safer architecture displaced attractive metallic-lithium energy density.
diffusionAndScaling: Diffusion depended on complements, cost/yield/standards and institutional adoption; the nominal breakthrough date did not equal broad effective use.
standardsAndInstitutions: Laboratories, firms, standard bodies, regulators, users and infrastructure operators owned different parts of evidence, implementation and consequence.
externalitiesAndCorrections: Lifecycle harms and authority changes are preserved where evidenced rather than inferred from local technical success.
secondOrderEffects: Commercial lithium-ion was a sequence of material and architecture corrections in which repeatable cycling and safety outranked locally maximal energy density.
sourceNativeSummary: Commercial lithium-ion was a sequence of material and architecture corrections in which repeatable cycling and safety outranked locally maximal energy density.
